newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FORECAST-Sweden March c/a seen 3.1 bln skr surplus.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Sweden March c/a seen 3.1 bln skr surplus.

text.p: Sweden's current account in March is expected to show a 3.1 billion crown surplus, a Reuter poll of 18 analysts showed on Friday.
Forecasts ranged from surpluses of two to four billion crowns. Behind the figure is the already published March trade surplus which came in at a strong 9.1 billion crowns, the analysts said.
A 3.1 billion crown current account surplus for the month of March would give an 11.8 billion crown surplus for the first four months of the year.
The current account balance for 1997 is expected to total 49.1 billion crowns, with estimates ranging from 35.3 billion to 55 billion crowns, according to the poll.
In February the current account showed a surplus of 3.3 billion crowns. In March 1996 it showed a surplus of 4.3 billion crowns and for 1996 it was a surplus of 40.2 billion crowns.
The Riksbank is due to publish the figure at 1000 GMT on May 22.

Analysts who participated in this survey were from Aragon, Carnegie, Consensus, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, Hagstromer & Qviberg, Handelsbanken, IDEA, J P Morgan, Lehman Brothers, Morgan Stanley, Nomura, Nordbanken, Paine Webber, Penser, S-E-Banken, Swedbank, Transferator, Unibank Markets and Ohman Fondkommission.
Only monthly forecasts: Consensus, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, IDEA, Lehman Brothers, PaineWebber, Swedbank, Unibank Markets.
